title: Natural termwise pullback counit on localized strictly perfect complexes
statement: Let g:T -> S be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], U an open of S and V its inverse image. On the localized module categories [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], write A and C for the open-site equivalences to modules on U.toScheme and V.toScheme. Write F for the ordinary localized pullback functor constructed in [lem-pc-localized-pullback-perfect-model], and L for the derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback] along V.toScheme -> U.toScheme. Choose localized derived categories with arbitrary independent universes w and wV, and scheme-open derived categories with a common universe wO [def-pc-derived-category]. There exists one natural transformation eta: Q followed by A.mapDerivedCategory followed by L -> F applied termwise followed by Q followed by C.mapDerivedCategory, on all complexes on the localized site over U. For every strictly perfect complex K [def-pc-perfect-complex], eta.app K is invertible. There are no bottom-degree or support hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 06YJ, natural derived counit on K-flat complexes; Tag 06YD, bounded-above flat K-flatness

proof.text: Read exists_derivedPullback for the restricted scheme morphism V.toScheme -> U.toScheme. Its recorded object and morphism equalities identify its ordinary functor with tensorPullback, and its canonical counit epsilon is natural on all homotopy complexes. Identify tensorPullback and ordinary module pullback by uniqueness of their left adjoints to the same pushforward.

Whisker epsilon with the homotopy quotient and compose the canonical quotientCompQhIso and mapHomotopyCategoryFactors isomorphisms. Then compose the termwise adjoint-uniqueness isomorphism. This constructs a natural transformation from Q followed by the restricted derived pullback to ordinary termwise pullback followed by Q.

Whisker that transformation with the source open-site equivalence and its derived localization factorization. The target open-site equivalence counit, functor associators, mapHomologicalComplexCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryFactors give a natural isomorphism identifying its target with localizedPullback followed by Q and the derived target equivalence. Composing its inverse gives eta on all localized complexes.

For a strictly perfect K, source open-site equivalence preserves boundedness, finite coproducts, unit objects, and explicit finite-free retract equations. The mapped finite-free terms are flat by flat_coproduct and flatness of the unit; flat_of_retract implies the transported K terms are flat. Install the tensorClosed structures and Grothendieck abelian module category to use these flat-object tools.

By bounded-above flat K-flatness, the transported K is K-flat. The K-flat clause of exists_derivedPullback makes epsilon at that complex invertible. Every other component used to construct eta is an isomorphism, so eta.app K is invertible. The same reasoning includes zero complexes, empty opens, and all independent localization universes in the statement.

lean.statement:
theorem localizedPullback_perfectCounit {T S : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S)
    (U : S.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wV}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings T.toRingedSpace).over (g ⁻¹ᵁ U)))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wO}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wO}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (g ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.toRingedSpace))] :
    let A : SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U) ⥤
        SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace) :=
      (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U).functor
    let C : SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings T.toRingedSpace).over (g ⁻¹ᵁ U)) ⥤
        SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (g ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.toRingedSpace) :=
      (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (g ⁻¹ᵁ U)).functor
    ∃ η : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ A.mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        derivedPullback (g.resLE U (g ⁻¹ᵁ U) le_rfl) ⟶
      (Scheme.Modules.localizedPullback g U).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          C.mapDerivedCategory,
      ∀ K : CochainComplex
          (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ,
        Scheme.IsStrictlyPerfect S U K → IsIso (η.app K)
